σημαίνει· οὕτω καὶ Ματθαῖον τοῦ τελωνείου ἀπολέσας ὁ Κύριος, δικαιοσύνην αὐτῷ
ἐχαρίσατο· πληθύνονται γὰρ οἱ δίκαιοι, ὅταν οἱ ἀσε βεῖς καταλείψωσι τὴν ἀσέβειαν,
καὶ σὺν τοῖς δι καίοις γενήσονται δίκαιοι· στένουσι δὲ καὶ οἱ δίκαιοι καὶ ὀδυνῶνται,
ὁρῶντες τοὺς ἀσεβεῖς ἐν τόπῳ τῆς ἀσεβείας ἱσταμένους, καὶ μὴ μετανοοῦντας.
Κρείσσων γὰρ ἀνὴρ ὁ ἐν παιδείᾳ καὶ νουθεσίᾳ Κυρίου ἐλέγχων, ἢ ὁ ἐν σκληρᾷ καρδίᾳ
παραινῶν καὶ ὑπισχνούμενος συναπολαῦσαι αὐτῷ τῶν ἐν κα κίᾳ· ἐξαπίνης γὰρ
φλεγομένου αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ ὀρέξει τῶν παθῶν, ὁ ἐπὶ πάντας θάνατος, ἐπελθὼν ἐπὶ τοὺς
κατ' αὐτῶν συμπράκτορας, οὐκ ἔστιν ἴασις τῇ ψυχῇ αὐτῶν· οὐκ εἶπεν δὲ, ὅτι
παυσαμένης τῆς φλογὸς οὐκ ἔσται ἴασις, ἀλλὰ φλεγομένου αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἔσται ἴασις, ὡς
ἔχοντος δηλονότι τὰ τῶν παθῶν ὑπεκκαύ ματα, ξύλα, χόρτον, καλάμην· εἴπερ καὶ
τοῖς καιο μένοις μετὰ τὸν καυτῆρα πέφυκεν ἡ ὑγίεια προσγί νεσθαι.
Ἐγκωμιαζομένων τῶν δικαίων ὑπὸ τοῦ Κυρίου ἐν τῇ
pass_a_gloss: This means the Lord called Matthew from tax work and gave him righteousness, since the just grow when the wicked turn from evil and join the zealous in righteousness. The just also sigh and sorrow, seeing the unrepentant wicked remain in wickedness. A man who corrects in the Lord’s training is better than one who urges with a hard heart, promising shared joy in the fire; for when he burns suddenly in passion’s desire, death overtook all comes on his accomplices, and no cure exists for their souls. He did not say cure comes after fire dies, but that none exists while it burns, since it clearly feeds on passion’s fuel—wood, grass, stubble—because if health returns after burning for those burned, so it is here. When the Lord praises the just on judgment day, their people will rejoice; but those under rulers, authorities, and world lords will then groan. Here he names God as Father; yet the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, seeing those named after Christ who follow in work, word, and wisdom and imitate Him, rejoices over them. The good shepherd is a mind holding calm thoughts; thus a rash thought is passionate, a sheep is calm; so the Lord places the goat-like on His left. Sheep right; irrational souls called goats; those with tares named tares; wheat-owners named wheat from skilled habit; as Paul says love isn’t arrogant—meaning the loving one. Christ lifts reason via commands; lawless Antichrist provokes humanity to ruin. Judgment teaches: deciding between two shows justice and avoids wrong; same for virtues, all good. Peter judges nations—taught world Christian faith and piety; Paul and later teachers. Base man: followers of Theodotus, Judas, Samosatene, likeminded. David laughs: they’ll say, see the man who made no God his helper. Blood-men demons: killed Christ’s folk by bloodshed; upright seek his soul—those wanting to act and grasp their own deeds and thoughts. Fool: unchecked anger; but this one partially restrained—angry only at burning matters. To the simple, say this: For the diligent, patience slowly removes anger. Law-keepers have the Lord as their guide in the reign; law-breakers lack guidance but face punishment. No one is naturally stubborn; if they understand yet disobey, true stubbornness would prevent right thought ever. This is Pharaoh: hardened against Israel, corrected not by words but lashes. Self-indulgence causes sin; all sinners serve sin; thus all indulgers serve sin. On judgment day, they will deeply regret themselves. The Lord brings low the proud, exalts the humble. Pride is evil; it breeds destructive hunger via evil in practitioners, on judgment day. But the glory from honoring God in song and obedience will glorify those who hunger for righteousness, since glory is obeying God’s commands, as the Lord promises: those who glorify Him, He glorifies. Evil generates pride in the rational soul. A thief is only the devil; one who splits loyalty — obeying some divine orders, doing some evil — self-hates, since slightness implies this.
pass_b_english:
This signifies that, just as the Lord called Matthew away from the tax office, He bestowed righteousness upon him; for the righteous increase whenever the wicked abandon their wickedness and become righteous along with those who are fervent in devotion. The righteous also groan and grieve, seeing the wicked standing in the place of wickedness, unrepentant. Indeed, a man who rebukes in the Lord’s discipline and instruction is better than one who urges in a hard heart, promising to share enjoyment with him in the burning; for when he is suddenly ignited in the desire of the passions, death that comes upon all arrives upon his fellow workers, and there is no healing for their souls. He did not say that healing would not exist after the fire is quenched, but that there is no healing while it burns, because it clearly has as fuel the substances of the passions—wood, grass, stubble—since, if it is true that health naturally grows after the burner for those who are being burned, then the same applies here. When the righteous are praised by the Lord on the day of judgment, the peoples of their share will rejoice; but those who are under the rulers and authorities, and the world-governors of this world, will then certainly groan. Here he speaks of the Father as God; but the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, seeing those who are called after Christ, following Him in deed and word and wisdom, and imitating Him, rejoices over them. And the good shepherd is a mind that possesses dispassionate thoughts; but if this is so, then a rash thought is a passionate thought, and a sheep is a dispassionate thought; therefore, the Lord sets those who are like goats on His left.

The sheep are on the right hand; he calls those who possess irrational souls goats, and in the same way he names those who have the tares among them tares, and those who possess the wheat, wheat, calling them by the name of their possession from the skilled and practiced habit of the hand; such also is what is said by Paul: Love does not boast, that is to say, the one who has love. Christ raises up the rational nature through his commandments, but the lawless Antichrist stirs up the human race toward destruction. In all things, judging is said to be teaching; for indeed, the one who judges between two or more concerning one thing teaches what is just and how to abstain from injustice; likewise, concerning virtues and every good thing, judging is said to teach; but a man here judging nations, he says, is Peter, who has taught the whole world the faith in Christ and godliness; and Paul, and the other teachers who came after; but a base man, those who follow Theodotus and Judas and the Samosatene and those of like mind with them; moreover, concerning the base man, David says: And they shall laugh at him, and they shall say: Behold the man who did not make God his helper. Men of blood are the demons, who have slain those living in Christ by shedding blood; but the upright will seek out his soul; these are those who wish to do and to understand what they themselves have practiced and conceived. Truly, the foolish man has an unrestrained temper; but this one is tempered in part, that is, becoming angry at things that are burning with passion. And toward the simpler ones, this must be said:

To those who are earnest, the one who through patience gradually consumes anger, bit by bit. To those who keep the law, the Lord will be an interpreter in the kingdom; but to those who break the law, there will not be an interpreter, but rather a punisher will be present. For no one is by nature hard-hearted; this is shown by the fact that, even if one understands, they do not obey. For the one who is by nature hard-hearted would never think anything correct at any time. I say this because of Pharaoh, who was hardened against Israel, and who was not instructed by words but by scourges. If indulgence leads to sin, and everyone who sins is a slave to sin, then everyone who indulges is a slave to sin. And on the last day, they will not grieve little over themselves. The Lord humbles the proud, but gives glory to the humble. —He says that pride is wickedness; and pride, along with the hunger it brings, causes destruction through wickedness to those who practice it, on the day of judgment. But to those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, the glory they gave God in hymns and by keeping His commandments will glory them. For glory is doing God’s commandments, as the Lord Himself says: “Those who glorify Me, I will glorify.” And wickedness begets pride in the rational soul.
